source_read: PMC HTML PMC6225734, full text (abstract, introduction, methods, results, Tables 1-7, discussion, limitations, conclusions, funding and conflict statements); Figures 1-4 (timeline, attitude items, setting frequencies, well-being plot) not needed for any claim; online supplement (correlation matrix) not read

claims.overstatement: None for the Haijen sentence. Two qualifiers: 'lower well-being' means any fall in the WEMWBS score from baseline to 2 weeks, with no threshold for a meaningful change, so some of the 85 falls will be measurement noise; and the 279 are those with both measurements, 43% of the 654 who started (reasons for dropping out not collected). 'The one study that measured well-being before and after' is the editors' statement about the literature; the authors call their design unique as of 2018 (Discussion > Strengths, 1st paragraph).
claims.note: 85/279 = 30.5% (recomputed; claim's 30 in 100 and magnitude's 30.5% agree). The paper gives no test statistics for the MEQ and CEQ comparison between the two groups, only that the means did not differ. The printed test for baseline well-being, F(277) = 6.95 with p < 0.001, is internally inconsistent (F(1,277) = 6.95 gives p of about 0.009).

anchors.locator: Results > Splitting participants based on change in well-being, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Split by change at 2 weeks: WEMWBS fell in N = 85, no change or a rise in N = 194 (279 with both measurements; 85/279 = 30.5%). Mean mystical-type (MEQ) and challenging-experience (CEQ) scores did not differ between the two groups (no statistics given). The only difference was baseline WEMWBS, lower in the no-change-or-rise group, printed as F(277) = 6.95, p < 0.001.

anchors.locator: Materials and methods > Study design, 1st paragraph; Results > Changes in well-being scores, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Prospective observational web survey with opportunity sampling and no comparison group; mean WEMWBS 49.0 (95% CI 48.3 to 49.7) at baseline, 52.6 (51.8 to 53.4) at 2 weeks, 51.8 (50.6 to 53.0) at 4 weeks.

anchors.locator: Discussion > Limitations, 3rd paragraph; Results > Demographics, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Attrition: 654, 535, 379, 315 and 212 completed the five surveys; reasons for dropping out were not collected and selection bias is acknowledged.

claims.overstatement: Mostly careful (associations, recalled vs prospective distinguished, attrition and post-hoc dose stated). Wording points: (1) 'planning to take a classic psychedelic on their own' can be read as 'alone'; the source means on their own initiative, and many were with others (ayahuasca 11%, retreats); suggest 'on their own initiative'. (2) 'were associated with none' rests on non-significance in a model of about 198 people; better 'showed no statistically significant association with any' (lifetime number of uses with mystical-type score: -0.144, p = 0.086). (3) 'moderate' and 'small' are the editors' labels for standardized coefficients from a multivariable model. (4) 'measured before the drug' rests on trust: survey 2 could be completed on paper and entered later, and timing compliance was not confirmed (Limitations, 1st paragraph).
claims.note: All Haijen numbers in the statement and magnitude recomputed or found: 48.3/28.8/11.1% of 379; set -0.324 (SE 0.070); recreation -0.224 (SE 0.081); clear intentions 0.180 (mystical), 0.155 (visual; rounds to 0.16), -0.134 (challenging, p = 0.088); set and mystical 0.014 (p = 0.835); absorption 0.215 (challenging), 0.347 (mystical); R2 0.324 (challenging). About 198: the GLM had 16 predictors plus intercept and error df 181, so N = 198 (I get the same as the editors' inference). 49.0 to 52.6 confirmed; 315 of 654 = 48% remained at 2 weeks (fewer than half: correct).

anchors.locator: Materials and methods > Study design, 1st paragraph; Participant recruitment and dissemination of the study, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Prospective web survey, opportunity sampling: adults 18+ intending to take a classic psychedelic in the near future through their own initiative, recruited by online advertisements (Facebook, Twitter, newsletters, drug forums including two Reddit forums); five surveys: 1 week before, 1 day before, 1 day after, 2 and 4 weeks after.

anchors.locator: Table 2 (drug type rows); Results > Demographics, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Of 379 reporting on the experience: LSD/1P-LSD 183 (48.3%), psilocybin 109 (28.8%), ayahuasca 42 (11.1%), DMT/5-MeO-DMT 12 (3.2%), mescaline 10 (2.6%), other 23 (6.1%). Survey sample sizes 654, 535, 379, 315, 212.

anchors.locator: Materials and methods > Survey 2: pre-state > Measures; Table 3 (Factor 1 'Set' and Factor 3 'Clear intentions' columns) and its note
anchors.extracted: Self-constructed items, 0-100 visual analogue scale, survey sent 1 day before. 'Set' loadings: comfortable 0.765, open 0.708, well prepared 0.648, anxious -0.635, good mood 0.619, ready to surrender 0.583, preoccupied with work or duties -0.392. 'Clear intentions': strong expectations 0.695, clear intention 0.694 (items answered by 386 and 326 of 535).

anchors.locator: Table 7, DV challenging experience; Results > Predicting challenging experiences, 1st paragraph; Results > Predicting visual effects (R2 sentence); Statistical analyses, last paragraph
anchors.extracted: All variables standardized. CEQ (rated in survey 3, 1 day after): set B -0.324 (SE 0.070, t -4.593, p < 0.001; text F(181) = 21.09); recreation component (fun/party, social, curiosity; rated at baseline 1 week before) -0.224 (SE 0.081, p = 0.006); clear intentions -0.134 (SE 0.078, p = 0.088); absorption 0.215 (SE 0.082, p = 0.010); dose 0.219 (p = 0.005). R2 = 0.324 for CEQ, 0.342 for MEQ, 0.211 for visual effects.

anchors.locator: Table 7, DV mystical-type experience and DV visual effects; Results > Predicting mystical-type experiences and Predicting visual effects
anchors.extracted: MEQ: absorption 0.347 (SE 0.076, p < 0.001), clear intentions 0.180 (SE 0.072, p = 0.013), set 0.014 (p = 0.835), dose 0.285 (p < 0.001), spiritual connection 0.153 (p = 0.054). Visual effects: clear intentions 0.155 (SE 0.072, p = 0.033), absorption 0.227 (p = 0.003), dose 0.327.

anchors.locator: Table 7 (trait rows, all three DVs); Discussion > Trait-variables as predictors for the acute psychedelic experience measures, 2nd paragraph
anchors.extracted: Openness, emotional stability, trait anxiety, suggestibility and stubbornness: no p below 0.05 for MEQ, CEQ or visual effects (trait anxiety and CEQ 0.140, p = 0.211); lifetime number of psychedelic uses: MEQ -0.144 (p = 0.086), CEQ -0.100 (p = 0.272), visual -0.116 (p = 0.167). Authors: no effects of the other traits found.

anchors.locator: Materials and methods > Statistical analyses, 6th paragraph; Survey 3 > Structure; Discussion > Limitations, 4th paragraph
anchors.extracted: Predictors in the acute-experience model: lifetime uses, 'highly experienced' item, six traits, three intention components, set, setting, clear intentions, dose, therapeutic environment; no drug type, no psychiatric history. Dose was estimated after the experience in five LSD-equivalent categories; the authors note the estimate may reflect the intensity felt. Error df 181 implies about 198 participants (16 predictors plus intercept).

anchors.locator: Results > Changes in well-being scores, 1st paragraph; Results > Demographics, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: WEMWBS mean 49.0 (95% CI 48.3 to 49.7) at baseline, 52.6 (51.8 to 53.4) at 2 weeks, 51.8 (50.6 to 53.0) at 4 weeks; population norm 50.7; quadratic trend F(154) = 23.20, p < 0.001; no comparison group; 315 of 654 (48%) completed the 2-week survey.

anchors.locator: Table 6 (mystical-type, trait anxiety, lifetime-use rows); Results > Traits, set and setting, intentions and acute psychedelic experience measures predicting well-being changes, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: With traits, intentions, set, setting, dose and acute measures in one model, MEQ x time: -0.102 (p = 0.887) at 2 weeks, 0.002 (p = 0.998) at 4 weeks; only trait anxiety (F(172) = 3.93) and lifetime uses (F(106) = 6.11) interacted with time. In the smaller model (Table 5), MEQ went with WEMWBS at 2 weeks (B 2.287, t(286) = 4.52).
Compliance with survey timing could not be confirmed; the pre-state survey could be completed on paper and entered later, taken on trust.

claims.overstatement: No overstatement; 'weak, uncertain' fits. One small inaccuracy: the retreat or therapeutic setting variable was not one yes-or-no item; survey 3 asked two separate yes/no questions (a psychedelic retreat? a setting designed or prepared with a therapeutic objective?), and the authors grouped people in a retreat with those reporting a therapeutic setting into one yes/no variable. Suggest 'reported afterwards as two yes-or-no questions combined into one variable'.
claims.note: Setting and CEQ: -0.137 (rounds to -0.14), SE 0.075, t -1.824, p = 0.070 in Table 7; the text gives F(181) = 3.33, p < 0.080 (t squared = 3.33, consistent). Therapeutic environment and CEQ 0.021, p = 0.813 (magnitude's 0.02, p = 0.81: correct). Not in the claim, possibly worth a clause: in the full well-being model the setting component went with higher WEMWBS at 2 weeks (B 1.206 per SD, p = 0.037; 4 weeks 1.216, p = 0.077).

anchors.extracted: 'Setting' component, rated 0-100 in the survey sent 1 day before: good feeling about relationship with the group or people who will be present 0.863, good relationship with the main person or people who will look after me 0.848, environment or setting feels good 0.604.

anchors.locator: Table 7, DV challenging experience ('Setting' row); Results > Predicting challenging experiences, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Setting and CEQ (rated about 1 day after): B -0.137, SE 0.075, t -1.824, p = 0.070; text: F(181) = 3.33, p < 0.080, described as a trend. Setting and MEQ -0.021 (p = 0.759), visual -0.058 (p = 0.400).

anchors.locator: Table 7 ('Being in a therapeutic environment' rows, three DVs); Survey 3 > Measures; Discussion > Set, setting, and drug dose as predictors for acute psychedelic experience measures, 3rd and 4th paragraphs
anchors.extracted: Therapeutic environment: MEQ 0.034 (p = 0.671), CEQ 0.021 (p = 0.813), visual -0.010 (p = 0.905). Two separate yes/no items (retreat; setting designed with a therapeutic objective) were asked after the experience; people in a retreat were grouped with those reporting a therapeutic setting; the term was not pre-defined for participants.

anchors.locator: Table 6 ('Setting' rows); Results > Traits, set and setting, intentions and acute psychedelic experience measures predicting well-being changes, 2nd paragraph
anchors.extracted: In the full well-being model, setting x time: 0.008 (p = 0.986) at baseline, 1.206 (SE 0.572, p = 0.037) at 2 weeks, 1.216 (p = 0.077) at 4 weeks, in WEMWBS points per SD.

key_findings.correction: Wording only: 'not associated' means no coefficient with p below 0.05 in a model of about 198 people (lifetime uses with mystical-type score -0.144, p = 0.086); 'no statistically significant association' would be more exact.

reporting_issues.note: F(2,232) = 3.03 gives p = 0.0502 (recomputed); with 1 df it would be 0.083, so on either reading it is not below 0.050.
Every Table 7 t squared matches the printed F (e.g. -4.593 squared = 21.10, text 21.09; 1.824 squared = 3.33); 181 + 17 parameters = 198.
r(653) = 0.22 is in Discussion > Acute psychedelic experience measures as predictors for change in well-being, 3rd paragraph; r(654) = 0.21 in the Discussion's 2nd paragraph (before the subsections).
Intercepts 49.716 (Table 5) and 50.329 (Table 6); standardization statement is the 7th (last) paragraph of Statistical analyses.
The Abstract makes the same statement ('baseline trait variables had the strongest effect').

risk_of_bias.note: ROBINS-E overall high is justified by unadjusted confounding (drug type, psychiatric history, other drugs) and heavy unanalysed attrition (about 198 of 654 in the acute-experience model).

interpretation_gap.note: 'Substantial' fits: causal verbs in the Abstract ('promoted', 'decrease the likelihood'), the Strengths claim about causal inference, the unsupported variance statement, and Implications turning associations into recommendations. Quoted Discussion phrase checked against the source.

missed: Discussion, 2nd paragraph: lifetime number of psychedelic uses correlated negatively with the change in well-being, r(279) = -0.23, p < 0.001 (people with more experience improved less), consistent with the lifetime-uses x time interaction in Table 6; relevant wherever the well-being rise is cited.

Discussion > Strengths, 1st paragraph: the authors describe the design as never before implemented in psychedelic research (as of 2018); the claims' 'the one prospective study' framing rests on this plus the editors' own knowledge of the literature, which the card could note under replication.
